lines.text: Jo bikes up a hill slowly, then zooms back down.
lines.caption: Jo bikes up a hill slowly, then zooms back down.

lines.text: Is her average just the average of the two speeds?
lines.caption: Is her average just the average of the two speeds?

lines.text: Jo bikes up a three kilometer hill at twelve kilometers per hour, then back down at ten meters per second.
lines.caption: Jo bikes up a three kilometer hill at twelve kilometers per hour, then back down at ten meters per second.

lines.text: What's her average speed in kilometers per hour?
lines.caption: What's her average speed in kilometers per hour?

lines.text: First fix the units. Ten meters per second is thirty-six kilometers per hour.
lines.caption: First fix the units. Ten meters per second is thirty-six kilometers per hour.

lines.text: Up takes fifteen minutes. Down takes just five.
lines.caption: Up takes fifteen minutes. Down takes just five.

lines.text: Six kilometers in twenty minutes. That's three times as far in one hour!
lines.caption: Six kilometers in twenty minutes. That's three times as far in one hour!

lines.text: Six times three is eighteen kilometers per hour!
lines.caption: Six times three is eighteen kilometers per hour!

lines.text: Averaging speeds is a trap. She's slow for longer!
lines.caption: Averaging speeds is a trap. She's slow for longer!

lines.text: Why is the average so low? The full lesson shows two ways, plus every trap.
lines.caption: Why is the average so low? The full lesson shows two ways, plus every trap.
